title: Cluster-State Witnesses of Finite-Speed Hidden Influences
authors: Weikang Li, Mengyao Hu, Dong-Ling Deng, Valerio Scarani
abstract: Bell experiments rule out local common-cause explanations of quantum correlations, yet they do not exclude hidden influences that travel faster than light while still having a finite speed in a preferred frame. Multipartite spacetime arrangements turn this possibility into a constraint: two late parties that are outside each other's hidden-influence cones must remain Bell-local once the earlier events are fixed. Here, we formulate this constraint as a projected-polytope separation problem for cluster-state correlations, using only marginal data containing at most one late party. From linear cluster states, we construct a four-qubit witness with the bound $S_4\le 6$ and quantum value $4+2\sqrt2$, and a five-qubit witness with $S_5\le 10$ and quantum value $6+4\sqrt2$. We certify that the exposed faces are facets of the corresponding projected hidden-influence polytopes. These results identify linear-cluster graph states as certifiable and experimentally friendly resources for finite-speed hidden-influence tests.
summary: The paper develops novel witnesses based on linear cluster states to test theories involving hidden influences that travel at a finite speed. By formulating this constraint as a polytope separation problem, the authors derive specific four- and five-qubit inequalities that violate these hypothetical models if measured values exceed theoretical bounds. This establishes cluster graph states as powerful resources for testing causality.
main_problem: To formulate a testable constraint for hidden influences that propagate at a finite speed, extending beyond standard Bell tests.
main_result: The authors derive new four- and five-partite witnesses using linear cluster states that certify bounds on these finite-speed hidden influence models.
method: The problem is formulated as a projected-polytope separation problem for cluster-state correlations, utilizing linear programming to find facet-defining inequalities.
model_or_system: The model considers hidden influences propagating at a finite speed (v) in a preferred frame, leading to constraints on multipartite spacetime arrangements. The quantum resource used is the linear cluster state ($|	ext{LC4}angle$ and $|	ext{LC5}angle$).

important_parameters: Finite speed $v$, number of parties (four or five qubits), and the specific structure of the cluster graph state.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes measurement independence, no postselection, and that the exposed faces are facets of the projected hidden-influence polytopes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the finite-speed causality geometry (v-cone vs. light cone) and show projections of the full polytope onto lower-dimensional spaces defined by the witnesses.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical constraint (HIC) to formulating it as a polytope separation problem, deriving specific cluster-state witnesses ($S_4, S_5$), proving their facet status using optimization techniques, and calculating quantitative bounds and visibilities.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, experimentally friendly quantum resources (linear cluster states) for testing fundamental assumptions about causality in physics beyond standard Bell tests, which is highly relevant to foundational quantum information theory.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Finite-speed causality geometry. The blue solid lines de- note the ordinary light cone, whereas the orange dashed lines de- note the wider hidden v-cone associated with a finite influence speed v > c in the preferred frame. The set E denotes the early side, whose measurement event(s) may influence both late parties B and C through the hidden influence. The late events are arranged out- side each other’s hidden v-cones, denoted by B ∼C, so no hidden influence can propagate between them during a run. Consequently, conditioned on every non-null input–output event on E, the BC dis- tribution must be Bell-local.

FIG. 2. Linear-cluster witnesses, visibility, and illustrative HIC projection. (a) LC4 uses the four-qubit chain with early side E = AD and blind late pair B, C. (b) LC5 appends E, giving E = ADE with the same blind pair. The BC link in each panel denotes a graph-state edge, not a causal connection; no witness term contains both B and C. (c) Ideal white-noise visibility, given by the ratio of the HIC bound to the quantum value SQ, with lower values indicating greater noise tolerance. (d) LC4 projection π4(P) := (R4(P), L4(P)). The fully Bell-local set L, hidden-influence set HICAD, and no-signaling set NS project to the inner square, intermediate octagon, and outer rectangle, respectively....
